Functions
With few exceptions, the redox-related reactions of NAD and NADP involve dehydrogenase (oxidoreductase) enzymes. As a family,
NAD and NADP-linked dehydrogenases constitute almost 20% of all classiﬁed enzymes and utilize about half of the cellular niacin
for their activation. The relative abundance of oxidized NAD(P)þ and the redox balance of NAD þ to NADH and NADP þ to
NADPH mediate the cell’s fate in a wide range of metabolic conditions. For example, decreasing the levels of NAD þ can inﬂuence
the rate of cellular apoptosis and, in the whole organism, the rate of malignancies, diabetes, and neurodegeneration. Thus, the ratio
of NADþ/NADH and NADPþ/NADPH may be viewed as redox couples that are signiﬁcant determinants of the cellular redox state.
